subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — plugin emission API and manifest policy

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this six-event public taxonomy and manifest-gated plugin emission capability as a supported SDK contract?
rationale: The permanent taxonomy, manifest permission model, trusted-plugin exception, and host capability boundary are public product and security decisions that cannot be established safely by patch repair alone.

options.title: Approve a host-bound API
options.body: Adopt the capability after replacing caller-controlled authority with a host-constructed emitter and completing parsing, validation, documentation, and live proof.

options.title: Keep taxonomy internal
options.body: Land only core-owned diagnostic contracts and defer third-party plugin emission until a narrower public capability design is approved.

options.title: Defer the series
options.body: Pause or close the stacked taxonomy work until operators and plugin authors have a confirmed product requirement and ownership plan.

recommendation.title: Approve a host-bound API
recommendation.body: Adopt the capability after replacing caller-controlled authority with a host-constructed emitter and completing parsing, validation, documentation, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent plugin contract and security-sensitive manifest reviews make this the strongest available routing candidate for the public API decision.
